title: endpoint SLI assertions and graded shedding simulator
creator: Ava Martinez
description:
Summary: Define a canonical set of per-endpoint SLI assertions (latency, availability, and request-quality) and implement a simulator that exercises graded load-shedding/circuit-breaker policies against historical traffic traces and synthetic surge scenarios. Goal is to surface robust error-budget accounting rules for multi-region failover and fallback crediting when model variants are used.

Scope:
- Formalize SLI expressions for: p50/p95/p99 latency, tail token latency, end-to-end availability, correctness/quality (route-specific metric like top-k match or embedding cosine similarity threshold), and per-request quality-weighted availability.
- Define how model variants (quantized vs full) are included in SLI aggregation and how variant-level error budgets are credited or debited.
- Policy for circuit-breaker thresholds (burn-rate, regional queue depth, per-tenant quota) and staged shedding actions (reject, degrade to cheaper variant, return cached prefix).
- Multi-region failover semantics: how error budgets are evaluated across origin and failover regions, and when to trigger region ejection vs redirect.
- Build a simulator that replays N-days of production traces (anonymized), injects synthetic spikes and region outages, and scores policy outcomes (SLO compliance, revenue delta, customer-visible error rate).
- Produce a runbook with operational thresholds and an enforcement plan for console automation (alerts, auto-rollbacks, and canary gating).

Artifacts and links:
- Design doc: https://drive.redwood.ai/docs/slo-sli-assertions-design 
- Simulator prototype PR: https://github.com/redwood-inference/slo-sim/pull/312
- Dashboard: https://console.redwood.ai/dashboards/slo-sim-results
- Example runbook draft: https://confluence.redwood.ai/display/OPS/SLO+assertions+runbook

Why now: Recent incidents where regional KV-cache misses plus model quantization regressions produced unexpected quality drops in failover paths. We lack a consistent way to credit fallbacks and it causes conservative regional ejections that impact cost and availability. This ticket centralizes rule definition and provides tooling to validate policies before rollout.
comments: 2026-02-22: Kickoff meeting notes posted. Present: Marcus, Ava, Priya (SRE), Diego (Model Ops). Action: Priya to export 14 days of anonymized traces for simulator (ETA 2026-02-26).

2026-02-27: Trace export completed. Initial data profiling shows 68% of requests are short-chat (<128 tokens), 18% long-form (>1024 tokens). Spike pattern correlated with APAC morning windows. - Marcus

2026-03-01: Prototype simulator v0.1 can replay traces and toggle regional latency profiles. Early run: naive breaker (95th latency > 1200ms) ejected region too aggressively; need burn-rate windowing. - Marcus
2026-03-03: Design review with PM and Design. PM recommends including a per-route quality SLA (top-1 match > 90% for rerank routes). Design flagged UX for showing variant-level SLOs in Console. - Ava

2026-03-06: Ran controlled surge test (2x requests, 1h) with three policies: reject-only, degrade-to-quantized, staged-eviction. Results: staged-eviction maintained effective availability (impact to quality 5%) while saving 22% cost vs reject-only. Uploaded CSV results to dashboard. - Marcus

2026-03-08: Engineering review feedback: unify SLI label naming to 'sli.latency.{quantile}', 'sli.quality.{metric}', 'sli.availability'. Ensure these map to telemetry tags for per-tenant attribution. Action: update exporter mapping. - Priya
2026-03-10: PM approval pending on accepted quality tradeoffs. Next: finalize acceptance criteria, run full 30-day replay with region outage scenarios, and prepare rollout canary. - Ava
acceptance_criteria: Canonical SLI spec published and merged into telemetry schema (p50/p95/p99 latency, end-to-end availability, route-specific quality metric)
Simulator repo contains reproducible runs and can import anonymized production traces; example runs for: traffic spike, APAC region outage, and model-variant regression
Policy matrix for circuit-breakers and staged shedding (thresholds, windows, actions) exists and has simulator-backed outcomes documented
Runbook with automated alerts and canary gating steps is reviewed and approved by SRE and Product
Console surfaces variant-level SLO breakdown and error-budget burn_chart for at least three representative routes
At least one canary rollout plan that uses simulator-backed thresholds is approved for runtime-1.28
